summary: Ephemeral connection shadowing reduces dedicated throughput for reserved pool during midday burst
description: Issue summary: Customer reports a sharp drop in throughput and elevated p99 during a midday traffic burst to their Dedicated reserved pool. Impact: sustained p50/p95 degradation for two hours, several request timeouts and an autoscaler cooldown that failed to provision additional GPUs. Environment: customer dedicated pool in us-east using pinned model versions. Initial observation suggested GPU shortages but allocation telemetry showed many slots were occupied by short-lived connections from a noisy tenant producing frequent reconnects (ephemeral streams).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer traffic pattern: many short-lived chatlet requests (~100-300 tokens) from multiple clients over a 30m window
2) Reproduce in staging by launching a burst of 10k short-lived connections with randomized keepalive intervals
3) Observe allocator and autoscaler metrics: slot occupancy, attach latency, and GPU attach failures
4) Check per-tenant connection counts and sidecar logs for repeated connect/disconnects
logs: grep of sidecar logs: conn_close reason=client_reset tenant=thirdparty-analytics multiple times per second
k8s events: Node gpu-123 preempted pods serving-sidecar-backfill OOMKilled=false
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Autoscaler cooldown prevented provisioning quickly enough during a burst. Evidence: autoscaler logs show repeated cooldown resets after failed attach attempts.

Hypothesis 2: Noisy neighbor (thirdparty-analytics) had a burst of short-lived connections causing slot fragmentation; many slots remained reserved by connections that didn't fully initialize model KV caches, reducing effective GPU throughput.
Metric analysis: p50 increased from 85ms to 320ms, p99 from 480ms to 2.1s between 12:00-14:00. GPU allocation failures rose from 0.2% to 7% during the window.
Tenant telemetry: thirdparty-analytics had 3.2k ephemeral connections during the 30m window, average lifetime 4.1s, peak connection churn 1200/sec.
Cluster state: 8/12 reserved GPUs attached, attach failures mostly in a subset of hosts showing high nvlink contention and high short-lived kernel thrash.
Reproduced in internal staging by simulating short-lived connection flood; observed same slot fragmentation and delayed autoscaler reaction under the default cooldown config.
comments: Ethan Zhao (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported throughput collapse at ~12:05. Collected logs and escalated to SRE.
Priya Patel (SRE) 2026-03-10: Investigating. Early signs point to short-lived connection flood from non-critical tenant causing slot hold. Will capture per-host conn profiles.

Miguel Torres (Platform) 2026-03-11: Tested simulated burst in staging. Autoscaler cooldown default (600s) prevents rapid scale; suggest temporary cooldown reduction and connection caps for the tenant.
Customer (LumenDocs) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reduced success rates during the window. Asking for root cause and permanent mitigations.

Priya Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Applied per-tenant ephemeral-conn cap to thirdparty-analytics in us-east as a temporary mitigation; reduced churn and recovered throughput to baseline. Monitoring shows p99 back to ~520ms.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporary per-tenant connection cap for noisy tenant in us-east and reduced autoscaler cooldown from 600s to 120s for the affected reserved pool. Long-term fix: platform change to enforce soft connection limits and improved attach backoff logic merged (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123). Customer notified and recommended to move non-critical analytics traffic to a separate pool. Follow-ups: schedule a config rollout (change-id CFG-2026-0315) to make cooldown tunable per-pool and add telemetry alert for rapid connection churn.
postmortem_action_items: 1) Product: expose per-pool autoscaler cooldown in Console (owner: Lina Gomez, ETA: 2026-03-22)
2) SRE: implement ephemeral-conn soft quota and throttling (owner: Priya Patel, PR merged)
3) Runtime: improve attach backoff to avoid repeated slot hold on short-lived connects (owner: Miguel Torres, ETA: 2026-04-05)
4) CS: notify affected customers of recommended traffic-shaping and offer migration assistance (owner: Ethan Zhao, ETA: 2026-03-16)
